feature: Alter company dates before financial entry
integration: Shared company edit workspace and confirmation dialogs, with a read-only target eligibility endpoint and a definitive revision/writer-locked mutation guard.

study.scope: Observed behavior of one new isolated fictional company containing no financial entries or opening balances
observed: Changing the saved financial-year beginning resets the Books draft to the new beginning.
Financial-year and Books-only changes each request two sequential confirmations before accepting the edited field.
No at either confirmation keeps the edited draft, returns focus to that field and does not advance or save. Discarding the form and reopening returns the last saved dates.
Both the financial-year change to 1-Apr-2025 and a Books-only change to 1-Jul-2025 persisted through save and reopen; the financial-year change was also verified across a real process restart.
Moving Books earlier within that year to 1-May-2025 was accepted and saved.
Books drafts before that year (31-Mar-2025) or after its end (1-Apr-2026) refused field advancement and form acceptance.
The already loaded working period and date were retained during date changes. A native process restart loaded the revised initial dates.
study.boundary: Warnings in an empty fixture do not establish deletion or migration behavior for existing financial records. No such behavior is implemented or inferred.

supportedScope.companies: Empty default and named companies. Preserve the default company's existing legacy posting-window policy.
supportedScope.financialEmpty: No rows in vouchers, postings, bills, receipt_allocations, ledger_openings, opening_bills, opening_bill_allocations, bill_terms, opening_bill_terms or journal_entry_order. A zero net balance does not mean empty.
supportedScope.masters: Existing master ledgers, their IDs/revisions and bank mailing metadata may remain; none are rewritten by the date operation.
supportedScope.restrictionOrigin: This empty-financial-record limit is an original Bookr capability boundary. It does not claim the reference app imposes the same restriction.
supportedScope.postedCompanies: Changed dates are rejected without mutation. Ordinary metadata edits with omitted or unchanged dates remain supported.

fields.financial_year_from: Existing ISO date, edited through the existing formatted date input
fields.books_from: Existing ISO date, edited through the existing formatted date input
fields.financial_year_to: Derived twelve-month end; no independently editable field
fields.revision: Existing positive catalog revision required for the mutation

api.capability: company_calendar_alteration: true in the existing capabilities responses

response.editable: Boolean from a read-only target-file check

eligibility.rules: Reject unsupported methods, query overrides, malformed/unknown IDs, missing files and incomplete unsupported book schemas. Do not construct a Book, seed tables, migrate files, activate the target or write catalog/book rows.
eligibility.authority: A true flag is advisory for rendering only. The PUT must repeat all validation and empty-record checks while excluding a target writer. A stale flag cannot authorize a mutation.

mutation.request: Existing metadata/date properties plus the current revision; no new date-only write endpoint
mutation.partialFY: A changed financial_year_from with omitted books_from resets Books to that new beginning.
mutation.explicitBooks: An explicit valid books_from overrides that reset.
mutation.omission: An unchanged or omitted financial-year beginning with omitted books_from preserves the saved Books value.
mutation.end: Always derive the end from the resulting financial-year beginning. A supplied end must match; do not preserve a stale old end during FY reset.
mutation.publication: Exactly one catalog revision increment and one committed metadata publication. Retry follow-up reads without repeating PUT.

validation: Use existing valid ISO-date and formatted-entry parsing, deriving the twelve-month end consistently.
Books must be within the resulting initial financial-year interval, including its existing inclusive boundaries.
Require the existing target identity, revision, supported stored-settings and unique-name checks.
Apply the financial-empty restriction only when the resulting date tuple changes; unchanged-date metadata updates keep existing behavior.
Never create a replacement for a missing company database or initialize an incomplete file as part of policy checking or metadata publication.

keyboard.Enter on changed FY: Reset Books, validate, then request the two original shared confirmations. No at either keeps both drafts and returns FY focus.
keyboard.Enter on changed Books: Validate and request the two confirmations. No at either keeps the Books draft and field focus.
keyboard.Ctrl+A or Accept: Validate and request any still-unaccepted date confirmations before saving. It cannot bypass them. Exactly one PUT follows final explicit acceptance.
keyboard.confirmationMemory: Acceptance belongs to the exact current date tuple. Editing it again invalidates acceptance.
keyboard.Escape: Keep existing editable-field clearing and company discard behavior. Escape in a confirmation is No.
keyboard.nextField: After explicit field acceptance continue the existing supported form navigation; configurable currency remains outside this increment. Whole-form acceptance remains a separate existing action.

ui.componentReuse: Use the existing shared confirmation component with original Bookr wording and existing date-entry helpers. When opening the second confirmation, preserve the actual edited field as cancellation focus rather than the removed first dialog button.
ui.noDeletionClaim: Do not copy a warning that data will be lost; this supported operation never deletes financial rows.
ui.olderBackend: Saved date inputs remain read-only if the new capability is absent. Static UI updates can coexist with an older running server.
ui.policyBinding: Enable date editing only if the policy's company_id and revision match the exact form profile and editable is true. Wrong-target, stale-revision, failed or unavailable eligibility reads cannot enable editing.
ui.savedResult: Keep canonical formatted dates, saved target ID/revision, disabled fields and the existing GET-only Refresh recovery after a successful PUT. Do not assign ISO dates through the metadata-only profile binder.
ui.failure: Rejected mutation keeps the unsaved draft and existing error path, with no navigation to another company.

storageAndCache.durableChanges: Only target catalog metadata/name/revision. No accounting/master/bank/sequence rows or schema are changed.
storageAndCache.guard: Keep catalog revision serialization and hold target writer exclusion across empty validation and publication. Do not touch a caller-owned transaction or present nested file transactions as all-or-nothing financial rewrites.
storageAndCache.cachePublication: After durable success, update the same cached Book object's calendar, opening date and posting-window configuration in place; retain its db connection. Pre-publication failure retains the old object/configuration.
storageAndCache.pendingRequests: A request that captured the Book before awaiting its body must use the committed new dates when it resumes. Closing/evicting that object is unsafe.
storageAndCache.otherStores: A later secondStore.book(id) lookup refreshes that store's cached object from the latest validated profile. No automatic cross-process update of arbitrary retained references is promised.

workingContext.loaded: Keep working-date and current-period tab bytes for already loaded companies, including an inactive target's retained context. The active company and other contexts do not change.
workingContext.reload: Tab reload retains Bookr's existing documented web-context convention.
workingContext.fresh: A fresh browser with cleared tab state uses the newly saved company calendar through the existing fresh-load model.
workingContext.distinction: Browser-tab retention is an original web convention, not a claim that a browser reload equals a native process restart.

backup: The same three stored date fields already belong to portable version1. Export committed dates with unchanged financial records and restore as a separate new UUID with exact master rows/sequences. Retain existing version1 compatibility and unsupported legacy-policy guards.
accountingEffect: None for the supported empty target. No vouchers, postings, bills, allocations, opening balances or master revisions are created/deleted/rewritten. The unrelated fictional 100000-paise sale less40000-paise receipt remains balanced with60000 paise outstanding.
